video_title: Davion Mitchell Is THE Davion Mitchell Type | Chris Mannix & Evan Turner

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Erik Spoelstra's tactical adjustments have diversified the Miami Heat's offense
quotes.excerpt: they made adjustments on the fly. They're doing a lot more dribble hand-offs, they're doing a lot more pick and roll.
quotes.quote: I'll give credit again to Eric Spoelstra and the coaching staff for some of the tweaks that they made. They made adjustments on the fly. They're doing a lot more dribble hand-offs, they're doing a lot more pick and roll. I think that's unlocked some things. They're not just playing downhill with Giannis anymore. They've diversified their offense, which I think has unlocked some stuff in Bam Adebayo, who had a great game 37 against Cleveland. Clay Thompson has been outstanding during this stretch. Giannis continues to be Giannis. Davion Mitchell proving everybody wrong. Anybody that thought Davion Mitchell could not be a starting point guard in the NBA, including me, I was one of them, proving people wrong.
quotes.social_post: Chris Mannix credits Erik Spoelstra for diversifying the Heat offense, moving away from relying solely on Giannis and unlocking Bam Adebayo and Davion Mitchell through more pick and roll and dribble hand-offs.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: The Miami Heat's turnaround is driven by collective team contributions
quotes.excerpt: now it seems as though everybody's stepping up, everybody's in the groove and they have a rhythm.
quotes.quote: I'm buying the Heat now due to the simple fact of the others. When we first started the season, it looked like it was just a one-man show. Obviously, Bam Adebayo was nowhere to be found, Clay was still trying to find his shot, Wiggins was still kind of on chill mode and you only had Davion Mitchell really showing up. Obviously, Giannis with his shots as well, but now it seems as though everybody's stepping up, everybody's in the groove and they have a rhythm.
quotes.social_post: Evan Turner says he is buying the Heat now that the team has moved past being a one-man show, noting that Bam Adebayo, Klay Thompson, and others are finally finding their rhythm alongside Giannis and Davion Mitchell.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Davion Mitchell is proving he can be a starting point guard
quotes.excerpt: not many people believed for years that Davion Mitchell could be a starting point guard.
quotes.quote: I want to key in on Mitchell for a minute. For a long time, Mitchell was like the guy you referenced when there was a college player coming out who was a little bit undersized. You said, well, he can make it because he's a Davion Mitchell type, which is really like a defensive bulldog who could be kind of a tweener in that backcourt, overcome a size disadvantage. Not many people believed for years that Davion Mitchell could be a starting point guard. But I was watching that Houston game, 16 points, 10 assist, he's playing that same brand of on-ball defense. He's just figured some stuff out and he's coming into his own as a playmaker in this league.
quotes.social_post: Chris Mannix admits he was wrong about Davion Mitchell, saying the guard is proving he can be a starting point guard in the NBA by combining his signature defensive bulldog style with improved playmaking.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Davion Mitchell's defensive presence disrupts opposing team's emotional leaders
quotes.excerpt: he was able to disrupt some of their emotional leaders.
quotes.quote: One thing with Davion Mitchell that makes him so impressive, when we thought the Rockets were unbelievable, it was like, hey, when you watch that game, it was like Giannis's presence was amazing, but it starts from the head of the snake and Davion Mitchell, even when it comes down to being able to guard Fred VanVleet, he was able to disrupt some of their emotional leaders. He was able to speed up and be like, hey, if I hit you right here, a gut punch, I know you guys are going to crack.
quotes.social_post: Evan Turner highlights Davion Mitchell's defensive impact, noting how he acts as the head of the snake by disrupting opposing emotional leaders like Fred VanVleet to force teams to crack.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Miami's success is tied to their high-percentage three-point shooting
quotes.excerpt: you've got Larsen shooting 47%, you got Mitchell shooting close to 44%, you got Clay Thompson at 43%.
quotes.quote: I keyed in before the season on the three-point shooting with Miami. You've got Larsen shooting 47%, you got Mitchell shooting close to 44%, you got Clay Thompson at 43%. These are not particularly small sample size, especially with Clay who's had nine and a half threes per game. You got guys that are making three-point shots and I mentioned Wiggins, he's not played well this season, there's still hope I'm sure there that he can improve his play. They've figured some stuff out too as well. I think for me, just like I talked about the top with Walker Kessler being like the wildcard with the Lakers going from good to great, I think the same thing about Davion Mitchell. I think you know what you're going to get from Giannis, you know what you're going to get from Bam, Clay may not be Warriors Clay, but he's still a pretty good player. If Mitchell can like play other point guards to like a standstill, they're good.
quotes.social_post: Chris Mannix points to Miami's high-percentage three-point shooting from Larsen, Mitchell, and Klay Thompson as a key factor in their success, calling Davion Mitchell the wildcard that could take the team from good to great.
